Lyric Motion Studio is a tool for creating kinetic-typography lyric videos from a song and its lyrics. Everything is processed inside your browser — your audio and lyrics are never sent anywhere.

  • Auto-direct: just pick a genre theme, and colors, fonts, layouts, motions, transitions, and backgrounds are composed automatically with a consistent look & feel
  • Timing: tap along during playback / "Start here" / per-word timing, latency compensation, and quantizing to the beat
  • Pro-grade export: MP4 / MOV / WebM / WebM with alpha / PNG sequence / GIF, chroma key, 23.976–60 fps, true motion blur, and batch export in multiple aspect ratios
  • Subtitle data: SRT / WebVTT / LRC (including extended LRC with word timing)

Recommended: the latest Chrome or Edge (desktop). Video export uses the browser's WebCodecs.

1. Add audio — Drop an MP3 / WAV / M4A, etc. into the box in the Assets tab. Tempo (BPM) and beats are analyzed automatically.
  2. Paste lyrics — Paste them one phrase per line and click Auto-place lyrics. Temporary timing is assigned based on volume and character count. If you have an LRC / SRT file, import it directly via "TXT / LRC / SRT".
  3. Pick a theme — In the Auto tab, click the theme closest to your song's genre. Switch with 🎲 (change seed) or "Previous / Next take" until you like it.
  4. Sync the timing — Turn on ● Tap timing in the timeline below and play. Press Enter when the vocal starts and release it when it ends (see "Timing" for details).
  5. Export — Choose a format from Export at the top right and save.

Your work is saved automatically in this browser (including audio). To move it to another device, use "File → Save with audio (.lmz)".

Left panel
Assets (audio, lyrics, credits) / Auto (themes, song structure, generate) / Design (looks, aspect ratio, colors, fonts, background motion) / Effects (global filters, BPM) / Phrases (fine-tuning, list)
Center
Preview. Drag text to reposition it; playback controls are below. Setting preview quality to "Auto" lowers resolution in heavy scenes to keep playback smooth (it doesn't affect export quality).
Right panel
Details for the selected phrase (timing, word timing, motion, layout, position, colors, font, effects).
Bottom
Timeline. The colored band at the top is the song structure, followed by the waveform, beat ticks, and phrase blocks (small vertical lines are word timings). Zoom with Ctrl+Wheel.

Ruby can be hidden all at once in "Design → Text & Motion". Markup symbols are removed automatically when exporting subtitles.

In the phrase editor, Enter inserts a / line break. Mixed Japanese/Latin lines match the Latin cap height and baseline to the Japanese face and keep Latin words tightly spaced. Straight quotes such as I'm and " become ’ “ ” automatically.

Tap timing (the fastest way)

Turn on ● Tap timing at the left of the timeline → play. Press Enter (or the on-screen TAP button) when the vocal starts, and release it when it ends. This sets the start of that line, and all following lines shift by the same amount. Use ↑↓ to go back to a line you want to redo.

"Start here" button

In the Phrases tab list, press Start here the moment a line's vocal begins during playback. The line snaps to the playhead and all later lines shift with it (Shift+I). Handy for fixing from a line in the middle. Even if later lines extend past the end of the song, they'll fit once you keep adjusting.

Latency compensation & quantize

  • Tap latency compensation: people press slightly after they hear the sound. Use "Measure" and tap along to the click to measure and compensate for your latency automatically.
  • Quantize: snaps starts (and optionally ends) to the nearest beat (1 beat, 1/2 beat, 1/4 beat, or bar start). Bar start uses the downbeat estimated from the audio. Use the strength % to just "nudge" toward the beat. "Auto-quantize on each tap" is also available.
  • Shift all: shifts all lines, or the selected line onward, by ± seconds.

Per-word timing (karaoke / word sync)

Turn on Per word next to Tap timing, and each press of Enter records the start of the next word (the first word also sets the line's start). In the right panel's "Word Timing", click a word chip to move the playhead to that word's time, or right-click to clear it. "Distribute evenly" and "Distribute on beats" are also available. Press W to mark the next word.

Word timings drive "Karaoke Fill", "Highlight Words in Sequence", word-based entrances (Word Slam, etc.), "Word Flash", and "Camera Track", keeping them perfectly in sync with the vocals.

Adjusting with the mouse

Drag a block in the timeline to move it, or drag its edges to set start / end. With Snap on, it snaps to beats, the playhead, and other lines' edges. The right panel also offers ±1-frame fine-tuning and "To beat".

Auto-place from vocals

🎤 Auto-place from vocals on the Assets tab analyses the vocals in your audio (the centre-panned voice) and estimates where each line starts and ends, plus the timing of each word. Everything runs in your browser; your audio is never uploaded.

  • If the lyrics match the current timing table line for line, only the timing is replaced and the styling is kept. 🔒 lines stay fixed and the rest is aligned around them.
  • Marking intro / interlude / outro sections in the song structure helps avoid mistaking those parts for singing.
  • If a lead instrument in the intro is mistaken for vocals and lines shift, select the first wrong line, press Start here at the moment the singing starts, then use 🎤 Re-align following lines to vocals. Everything after it falls into place.
  • Low-confidence lines are marked yellow in the phrase list — play them back to check.

It relies on the centre of a stereo mix, so accuracy drops for mono audio or songs where other instruments play loudly in the centre.

Mark Intro / Verse A / Pre-chorus / Chorus / Interlude / Bridge (C) / Bridge / Outro, and Auto-direct switches the tone per section.

  • In the chorus, motion intensity, background layering, and font changes are at their peak.
  • Background scenes in sections without lyrics switch on the start of each bar (the downbeat) estimated from the audio.
  • Repeat choruses (sections of the same type) reproduce the look of the first one for a unified MV feel.
  • A transition (cut) is always inserted at section boundaries.

Estimate from audio detects sections automatically from volume changes (labeled "estimated" — just a rough guide). In the band at the top of the timeline: double-click = add / click = change type / drag = move / right-click = delete. Press M to add at the playhead. After making changes, click "Auto-direct" to apply them.

A theme is a "narrowed-down set of candidates". It holds candidates and weights for layouts, enter / hold / exit motions, filters, transitions, accent graphics, background motions, fonts, and colors, plus motion speed (tempo feel). If the audio has been analyzed, more intense sections get bolder styling.

  • Seed: the same lyrics and seed always give the same result. 🎲 gives another take. Move between them with "Previous / Next take".
  • 🔒 Lock: lock the lines you like so they aren't regenerated (L).
  • 🎲 Re-roll: regenerates just that line (R).
  • "Auto colors", "Auto effects", "Transitions", and "Accent Graphics" can each be turned on or off.

Motion character

Keep your theme and adjust Intensity (calm to wild), Motion feel (smooth / bouncy / snappy / glitch / cinematic / organic / kinetic) and Variety (consistent to varied). Intensity steers the choice of enter/exit motions, camera, transitions and effects, plus motion size and speed. With “Apply changes instantly” on, the show is regenerated with the same seed as soon as you release a slider (🔒 lines are kept). “Reset to theme” restores the theme’s own settings.

Looks
Save colors, fonts, background, background motion, filters, and motion intensity/speed under a name and recall them with one click. Export as JSON to share with others. Great for managing guidelines per project or artist.
Aspect ratio
16:9 / 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5 / 4:3 / 3:4 / 21:9. Layouts are automatically redone when you change the ratio.
Colors
70+ palettes (monochrome, neon, pastel, retro, traditional Japanese, cinema, pop, edgy, etc.). Custom palettes are supported too. "Show keywords in the accent color" color-codes important words automatically.
Fonts
About 30 Japanese and about 45 Latin fonts from Google Fonts (sans serif, serif, script, tech/retro, display). You can also add your own fonts (TTF/OTF/WOFF), available only in that browser.
Mixing Japanese and Latin text
When a Japanese font is selected, Latin letters, numbers, and symbols (. , " ' ! ? etc.) are automatically set in a well-matched Latin font (Gothic → Inter, Mincho → Cormorant, Rounded Gothic → Nunito, etc.). Change it to any Latin font with "Latin font", and fine-tune its size with "Latin size". Also:
• Quote direction is detected automatically, so the " in "Don't stop" stays attached to its word and isn't left stranded at the start or end of a line.
• Japanese–Latin spacing: a 1/4 em gap is added automatically between Japanese and Latin text (not where you've typed a space).
• Japanese punctuation compression: 「」（）、。 are set at half width to remove loose gaps around brackets.
• Latin text uses pair kerning for optimal spacing. In vertical text, English words are rotated sideways, and , . within Japanese text are placed in the punctuation position.
Background images (multiple)
Add as many photos or illustrations as you like in "Design → Background Image" (drag & drop supported).
• Switching: Auto (at song structure markers, or every few phrases if there are none) / per phrase / per bar / manual (set an image per line in the right panel). Toggle anytime with "Use background images", click a thumbnail to toggle it individually, reorder with ◀▶, and double-click to adjust the focal point.
• Transitions: 19 types — Dissolve, Film Burn, Ink Dissolve, Iris, Diamond, Diagonal Light Wipe, Blinds, Tiles, Doors, Push, Stack, Whip, Zoom Through, Glitch, Pixelate, RGB Split, Flash, Spin Zoom, and Shutter (shatters into triangles). Auto picks each time from a family that suits the theme (soft / shape & slide / dynamic). Duration is "1 beat (auto)" or in seconds.
• Texture: As is / Vivid / Fade / Monochrome / Duotone (match palette) / color grading. Darkness, blur, slow zoom & pan, and beat pulse are also adjustable.
• While an image is shown, full-frame background motions (shaders, etc.) are automatically toned down (you can still stack them), and only overlay types like particles and light are layered on top.
Background motion
110+ types: particles, weather, water, fire, light, glitch, split screen, op art, typo wallpaper, ink marble, diamond tiles, gradient tubes, prisms, liquid metal, light leaks, anamorphic flares, 8mm film, light trails, Swiss grit (collage), GPU shaders (tunnels, kaleidoscopes, etc.). Stack up to 3. Use "Darken" to keep text readable.
Sections without lyrics (Intro, Interlude, Outro)
Sections where no lyrics are shown are detected automatically; background motion that fits the theme switches every bar, with a slow zoom and beat shake added. For the foreground you can choose "Circular Spectrum (audio-reactive)", "Scrolling Title Marquee", or "Title / Artist display", and a progress bar for the section is also shown. Section names like INTRO, INTERLUDE, and OUTRO can be toggled with "Show section names". Turn on "Countdown before vocals" to show ●●● and the next lyric starting 3 beats before it (great for karaoke). You can also fix the background with "Set background for instrumental sections…". These sections appear as hatched bands in the timeline.
Tempo feel
Motion speed. Turn on "Match motion duration to the song's BPM" to snap enter/exit durations to 1/4–3 beats and sync sway/bounce cycles to the tempo.

Background videos

The background library also accepts videos (MP4 / WebM / MOV). They switch, transition, and take looks and blending just like photos, and each clip has its own Range (start–end seconds), Playback (from the start at each switch / locked to song time), Speed, Loop and Zoom & pan. The preview plays along with the song, and export decodes the video frame-accurately. The clips’ own audio is not used.

Videos are stored in this browser and bundled into .lmz files (large clips use a lot of storage). H.264 MP4 or WebM is recommended.

Spacing

The Spacing block on the Design tab lets you set the type by hand: Spacing (Japanese / overall), Latin tracking, Word space, JP–Latin gap and Punctuation squeeze (around 「」、。). Use the sliders or − / ＋ to tighten or loosen; “Reset” restores the defaults.

To adjust one line, use Spacing / Word space in the detail panel, or select the line and press [ / ] (spacing, Shift for bigger steps) or Alt+[ / ] (word space). With several lines selected they all change, and the values are included in copy / paste style.

In vertical layouts, Latin text is rotated 90° and gets the same word spacing and kerning as horizontal text. Auto direction never picks the vertical layout for mostly-Latin lines.

Background motion blending

Use Opacity and Blend mode (Normal, Screen, Add, Lighten, Color dodge, Overlay, Soft light, Hard light, Multiply, Darken, Difference, Exclusion, Luminosity, Color) to control how background motion sits on top of your background image or background. The same settings appear under both Background motion and Background images on the Design tab. When you add your first image, it switches to “Screen · 60%” so the image stays visible.

Image / video blending

Background images and videos have their own Opacity and Blend mode, which control how they sit on the plain Background (color, gradient, pattern) underneath. This is a separate setting from background-motion blending. The stacking order is Background → images/videos → background motion → lyrics. The image Blend and Blur are image-only settings too and are stored separately from the Background section's Darkness and Blur.

Background-motion blending can be overridden per phrase (inspector) and per section. Overridden controls show an Override badge, and the global controls show a notice when other values are in use, with a button to clear all overrides.

Make background images / videos the star

Turn on Make background images / videos the star in the background image section and auto direction only picks background motions that don't cover the picture (particles, light, lines…). How much of the frame each motion covers is measured automatically. It also avoids effects that repaint or hide the image (two-tone, duotone, scanlines, letterbox…) and layouts that fill the screen with text, blends background motion with Screen at 50%, sets Blend to 15% and adds a soft shadow to the lyrics. It turns on automatically when you add your first image or video. Re-apply swaps covering background motions in the current direction.

Intro / interlude / outro settings

In “Sections without lyrics” on the Design tab, choose Section to edit: “All sections” or a single section (intro, interlude 1, outro…) — or click its hatched band on the timeline. Each section can have its own background choice, strength and speed, opacity and blend mode, camera motion, scene-change interval, change flash, foreground style and opacity, section name (e.g. GUITAR SOLO), progress bar and countdown. Anything you don’t change follows “All sections”; “Reset this section” clears the overrides.

Lyric lines can also override background-motion Opacity and Blend mode in the detail panel, under Background motion (↺ returns to the global setting).

• Motion: choose Enter → Hold → Exit separately (hover over a card to preview the motion). "Apply to all lines" is also available.
  • Layout: Center, Giant Poster, Vertical Text, Word Flash, Camera Track, Ring Repeat, Angular Tunnel, Repeat Full Stack, Card Deck, Brutalist Editorial, Typo Tiles, and more.
  • Transition: the effect at the moment the previous line switches to this one. 50+ types including Paper Tear, Slice Bands, Pixel Sort, Melt, Liquid Drip, Splash, Color Burst, Hexagon, Diamond Tiles, Ink Blob, Hand-drawn Scribble, Dry Brush, Collage, Gradient Ribbons / Circles, Light Leak, Doors, Prism, Film Advance, Zoom Twist, Whip, and Zoom Through.
  • Accent Graphics: hand-drawn ×'s & stars, strikethrough, sticker, rotating badge, meta info, ring burst, and more (up to 2).
  • Position, size & motion duration: use the sliders, or drag the text directly on the preview (Shift locks the axis, double-click centers it). Enter/exit durations can also be fixed in seconds.
  • Colors, font, size & effects for this line: can be overridden per line.
  • Copy / paste style: Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+V.
  • Multi-select: in the list or timeline, Shift+click = range, Ctrl (⌘)+click = add. Ctrl+A selects all. Changes to motion, layout, transition, and background motion, as well as Paste Style, Re-roll, Lock, and Delete, apply to all of them at once.
  • Title card: "＋ Title Card" in the Phrases tab inserts the title / artist into the gap at the start of the song (not included in subtitle exports).
  • Typographic motions: Weight motions change the letter weight (thin to bold landing, heavy punch-in, rippling weight, bolder on the beat, sung letters turn bold, thin out and vanish); Path motions move text along curves and arcs (flow in along a curve, unbend from an arc, sway on an arc, travel along a wavy line); plus mask reveals per character or word, per-character focus pull and spring.
  • Vocaloid PV motions: 90° roll-in/out, stepped zoom (dropped frames), invert flash, RGB split, sweeping bars, resolve from TV static, choppy frame shake, tilt / color / caption bar switching on the beat, caption bars and more. The Vocaloid theme uses them automatically.

There are global effects and per-line effects (per-line settings can also "Disable all" global effects).

Vocaloid PV style: background motions “HUD rings”, “Speed lines (pulse on the beat)”, “Flickering glyph tiles”, “Shape bursts”, “Oscilloscope waveform”, “Hazard stripes”, “TV static” and “Two-tone rotating split”; decorations behind the text “Grid paper”, “Scattered garbled glyphs”, “Shapes pop on the beat”; in front “HUD frame” and “Warning tape”; and screen effects “Two-tone (negative flip on the beat)”, “Quad mirror”, “Mosaic on the beat”, “Dropped frames”, “Zoom on the beat” and “Line art”. The Vocaloid theme combines them automatically (Quad mirror is never picked automatically because it makes lyrics hard to read).

"Intensity" controls the overall strength. Each effect can also be adjusted individually with its slider. For beat sync (BPM), you can enter it manually or use tap tempo in the Effects tab.

  • Background: Normal / Transparent / Green Screen / Blue Screen / Custom color. With Transparent, you can choose "Include decorative effects like particles and light".
  • fps: 23.976 / 24 / 25 / 29.97 / 30 / 50 / 59.94 / 60 (exact support for broadcast and film fractional rates).
  • Motion blur: true shutter blur (180°) that blends multiple moments into each frame. Fast motion looks more filmic (export time is multiplied by the sample count).
  • Also export other aspect ratios: 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, etc. in one go. Layouts are automatically rebuilt for each ratio.
  • Write directly to disk (local version): no running out of memory, even for long or 4K videos.
  • Range: "Whole song / Selected phrase / Custom". Export always renders at the highest quality, regardless of the on-screen preview quality.

Bringing it into your editor

  • After Effects: import the PNG sequence (alpha) via "File → Import → PNG Sequence". Set the frame rate to match the export.
  • Premiere Pro / DaVinci Resolve: WebM with Alpha or PNG sequence. Chroma key versions can be keyed with "Ultra Key" / "3D Keyer".
  • Final Cut Pro: import the PNG sequence, or use the chroma key version with the "Keyer".
  • Subtitles via "File → SRT / WebVTT"; for karaoke, "LRC (with word timing)".
  • YouTube chapters: creates description text like "0:00 Intro / 0:15 Verse A…" from the song structure (also copied to the clipboard).

• Auto-save: your work and audio are saved automatically in this browser and restored the next time you open it.
  • JSON: saves only the project (styling and timing). Lightweight and good for sharing (audio not included). Ctrl+S
  • .lmz: a package that includes the audio. Use it to move to another computer.
  • Import LRC / SRT: bring in timing made in other tools as is. LRC with word timing (<mm:ss.xx>) is also supported.
  • Snapshots: "File → Save / Restore snapshot" saves named versions you can return to anytime. They're also saved automatically right before auto-placing, generating, or restoring.
  • Undo / Redo: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z (up to 120 steps).
  • Reset settings to defaults: File → Reset settings to defaults… puts theme, colors, fonts, motions, effects, background motion and other settings — plus per-phrase overrides — back to their defaults. Lyrics, lyric timing, the loaded song, song structure & BPM, background images & videos, screen size, title & artist and saved looks are reset only if you check them (unchecked items are kept). A snapshot is saved automatically first.

Use 🌐 Language at the top right to switch the interface between 日本語 / English / Español / Italiano / 한국어. Your choice is remembered, and this manual is shown and saved in that language.

Lyrics can be written in any of these languages; typesetting detects the script automatically.

  • English, Spanish, Italian: lines break at word spaces, and accented letters (é à ñ ì…) are set in the Latin font. ¿ ¡ « stay with the next word and » ? ! with the previous one; apostrophes like l'alba stay in one word.
  • Korean: Hangul breaks at spaces. With a Japanese or Latin main font, only the Hangul is set in the Hangul font (Design tab). “Auto” matches the mood of the main font (sans / serif / display / handwriting). You can also pick a Korean font as the main font.
  • Word-by-word layouts such as Word Flash keep the spaces when they group short words, and auto-placement weights Latin text by reading length rather than raw character count.

Switching the display language never changes your project or lyrics. The first-run sample uses lyrics in the selected language.

<dl>
<dt>I chose MP4, but it says VP9</dt><dd>Your browser doesn't support H.264 encoding in this environment. Try the latest Chrome / Edge, or choose WebM.</dd>
<dt>My taps are always slightly late</dt><dd>Measure your latency with "Phrases → Tap latency compensation → Measure". You can also snap to the beat with "Quantize".</dd>
<dt>The preview is choppy</dt><dd>Set preview quality to "Auto" or "Light". This doesn't affect the exported result. Reducing GPU shader backgrounds and heavy effects also helps.</dd>
<dt>The font doesn't change / shows boxes</dt><dd>Fonts are loaded from the internet. When offline, your device's Japanese fonts are shown instead.</dd>
<dt>The text is hard to read</dt><dd>Try raising "Darken" for the background motion, changing the colors, adding the "Outline" or "Drop Shadow" text decoration, or setting background motion to "None" per line.</dd>
<dt>I exported with transparency, but the background is black</dt><dd>Some players show transparent areas as black. It will be transparent when imported into an editor. PNG sequences are the most reliable.</dd>
<dt>Some lines extend past the end of the song</dt><dd>This is a temporary state during adjustment. Sync the lines in order from the earlier ones and they'll fit. The overflow isn't included in the export.</dd>
</dl>

1. Add the audio and lyrics, estimate the song structure, then check and fix the band.
  2. Choose a theme, settle on a direction with 🎲, then save it as a look (for the project's guidelines).
  3. Sync the lines with Tap timing, then tighten them with latency compensation + quantize.
  4. Use per-word timing only on the chorus and key lines to set up word-synced effects.
  5. Multi-select the showcase lines, unify them with the same motion and transition, and 🔒 lock them. Adjust the rest by regenerating.
  6. Export an MP4 (30 fps) for client review, and the final as a PNG sequence (alpha) + motion blur for AE. For social, use batch aspect ratios to export 9:16 / 1:1 at the same time.
